title: Sum of Numbers Hit by 3, 5 or 7
statement:
Given a positive integer n, add up every integer in 1..n (inclusive) that is divisible by at least one of 3, 5 or 7. Each such number is added once, even if it is divisible by several of them. Return the total.

Our version allows n up to ten million, so a loop over every number is too slow in the big test.

examples.why: Add 12, 14 and 15 to the previous list. 15 is divisible by both 3 and 5 but counts once.
Neither 1 nor 2 is divisible by 3, 5 or 7.

hints: The sum of the multiples of k up to n is k · (1 + 2 + … + m) with m = ⌊n / k⌋. That has a closed form.
Adding the sums for 3, 5 and 7 counts numbers like 15 twice. What do you subtract to fix that?
Inclusion–exclusion: S(3) + S(5) + S(7) − S(15) − S(21) − S(35) + S(105).

explain.intuition:
The multiples of k up to n are k, 2k, …, mk with m = ⌊n/k⌋, and their sum is k · m(m+1)/2. Adding that for 3, 5 and 7 overcounts numbers divisible by two of them, so subtract the sums for 15, 21 and 35. Now numbers divisible by all three (multiples of 105) were added three times and removed three times, so add them back once.

That is inclusion–exclusion, the same counting rule as the size of a union of sets. Seven closed-form sums replace a loop over ten million numbers.
pitfalls: Stopping after subtracting the pairs. Multiples of 105 then count zero times instead of once (try n = 105).
Subtracting the pairwise overlaps only once in total, or using 3·5·7 in place of the pair products.
Integer overflow in languages with 32-bit ints: at n = 10⁷ the answer is about 2.7 · 10¹³.

solutions.title: Check every number
solutions.idea: Loop over 1..n and add the numbers divisible by 3, 5 or 7.

solutions.title: Inclusion–exclusion with arithmetic series
solutions.idea: Sum multiples of each divisor in closed form, then correct for double and triple counting.

followups: The divisors are an arbitrary list of up to 15 numbers. How do you generate the inclusion–exclusion terms, and why do you need lcm instead of the product?
Count the numbers instead of summing them. What changes?
